body_markdown:
# Introduction

A strong English vocabulary does not begin with difficult words. It begins with useful words that you can understand, remember and use in everyday situations. Learn a small group at a time, make your own sentences and revise the words regularly.

This lesson gives you 100 beginner-friendly words grouped by topic. The meanings are simple and the examples show how the words are used in sentences.

## 1. People and family

| Word | Simple meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| person | a human being | She is a kind person. |
| man | an adult male | The man is waiting. |
| woman | an adult female | The woman is a teacher. |
| child | a young person | The child is playing. |
| family | people related to one another | My family lives in Pune. |
| mother | female parent | My mother is at home. |
| father | male parent | My father reads the newspaper. |
| brother | male sibling | My brother is a student. |
| sister | female sibling | My sister likes music. |
| friend | someone you know and like | He is my good friend. |
| teacher | a person who teaches | Our teacher explains clearly. |
| student | a person who studies | The student is reading. |
| neighbour | a person living nearby | Our neighbour is helpful. |
| guest | a person invited or visiting | The guest has arrived. |
| worker | a person who works | The worker is careful. |
| doctor | a medical professional | The doctor is busy. |
| driver | a person who drives | The driver stopped the bus. |
| customer | a person who buys a service or product | The customer asked a question. |
| manager | a person who manages work or people | The manager is in a meeting. |
| team | a group working together | Our team starts at nine. |

## 2. Home and everyday things

| Word | Simple meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| house | a building where people live | Their house is small. |
| room | a part of a building | My room is clean. |
| door | an entrance that opens and closes | Please close the door. |
| window | an opening for light and air | Open the window. |
| table | furniture with a flat top | The book is on the table. |
| chair | a seat for one person | Please take a chair. |
| bed | furniture for sleeping | The bed is comfortable. |
| kitchen | a room for cooking | My mother is in the kitchen. |
| water | a liquid we drink | Please give me some water. |
| food | things people eat | The food is ready. |
| cup | a small drinking container | This cup is clean. |
| plate | a flat dish for food | Put the plate here. |
| spoon | a tool used for eating or serving | I need a spoon. |
| bag | something used to carry things | My bag is heavy. |
| phone | a device used to communicate | My phone is charging. |
| book | pages with written or printed information | This book is useful. |
| pen | a tool used for writing | Where is my pen? |
| key | a tool for opening a lock | I cannot find the key. |
| light | brightness from a lamp or the sun | Turn on the light. |
| clothes | things people wear | My clothes are dry. |

## 3. Common action words

| Word | Simple meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| go | move to another place | I go to work. |
| come | move towards the speaker or a place | Please come here. |
| eat | take food | We eat lunch at one. |
| drink | take a liquid | Drink enough water. |
| read | understand written words | I read every morning. |
| write | make words or letters | Write your name. |
| speak | say words | Speak slowly, please. |
| listen | pay attention to sound | Listen carefully. |
| see | notice with your eyes | I can see the bus. |
| look | direct your eyes at something | Look at the board. |
| make | create or prepare | Make a simple sentence. |
| take | get or carry something | Take your bag. |
| give | hand something to someone | Give me the book. |
| work | do a job or task | I work in a hospital. |
| help | make something easier for someone | Please help me. |
| open | move something so it is not closed | Open the door. |
| close | shut something | Close the window. |
| start | begin | The class starts now. |
| finish | complete | I finish work at six. |
| learn | gain knowledge or a skill | I learn English daily. |

## 4. Describing words

| Word | Simple meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| good | pleasant or suitable | This is a good idea. |
| bad | not good | The weather is bad. |
| big | large in size | It is a big room. |
| small | little in size | I have a small bag. |
| new | recently made or obtained | This is my new phone. |
| old | having existed for a long time | That is an old building. |
| easy | not difficult | This question is easy. |
| difficult | not easy | English spelling can be difficult. |
| happy | feeling pleased | I am happy today. |
| sad | feeling unhappy | She looks sad. |
| tired | needing rest | I am tired after work. |
| busy | having a lot to do | The doctor is busy. |
| clean | not dirty | Keep your room clean. |
| dirty | not clean | These shoes are dirty. |
| fast | moving quickly | The train is fast. |
| slow | moving without speed | Please speak slowly. |
| hot | having a high temperature | The tea is hot. |
| cold | having a low temperature | The water is cold. |
| early | before the expected time | I arrived early. |
| late | after the expected time | Do not be late. |

## 5. Time, place and useful words

| Word | Simple meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| today | this day | I am free today. |
| tomorrow | the day after today | I will call tomorrow. |
| yesterday | the day before today | I was busy yesterday. |
| morning | the early part of the day | Good morning. |
| evening | the later part of the day | See you this evening. |
| night | the dark part of the day | I sleep at night. |
| now | at this moment | Come here now. |
| later | after some time | We can talk later. |
| here | in this place | Please wait here. |
| there | in that place | Put the box there. |
| inside | in an enclosed place | The keys are inside. |
| outside | not inside | Wait outside. |
| near | close to something | The shop is near my house. |
| far | at a great distance | The station is far away. |
| always | every time | She always helps me. |
| sometimes | on some occasions | I sometimes walk to work. |
| never | not at any time | He never drinks coffee. |
| very | to a high degree | This book is very useful. |
| because | gives a reason | I stayed home because it rained. |
| but | introduces a contrast | I am tired, but I will study. |

## How to remember new words

Do not try to memorise all 100 words in one day. Use this five-step method:

1. Learn ten words from one group.
2. Read the meaning and example aloud.
3. Cover the meaning and try to remember it.
4. Write five original sentences using the words.
5. Revise the same words the next day and again after one week.

Keep a vocabulary notebook with three columns: **Word**, **Meaning**, and **My sentence**. Your own sentence helps you remember how a word works in real communication.

## Common vocabulary mistakes

- **Learning only translations:** A translation can help, but also learn an English example sentence.
- **Confusing similar words:** *Look* means direct your eyes; *see* means notice with your eyes; *watch* usually means look at something for a period of time.
- **Memorising too many words at once:** Learn fewer words and use them actively.
- **Ignoring word forms:** *Help*, *helps*, *helped* and *helping* are related forms. Notice how the form changes with the sentence.

## Practice: Use the words

Fill in each blank with the best word.

1. Please close the ____ before you leave. (door / water)
2. I ____ English every day. (learn / cold)
3. My ____ is a doctor. (mother / table)
4. The tea is very ____. (hot / near)
5. I will call you ____. (tomorrow / chair)
6. Please ____ carefully. (listen / kitchen)
7. This question is not difficult. It is ____. (easy / dirty)
8. The keys are ____ the bag. (inside / happy)

### Answer key

1. **door** — A door can be opened or closed.
2. **learn** — Learn is an action verb.
3. **mother** — Mother is a family word.
4. **hot** — Hot describes temperature.
5. **tomorrow** — Tomorrow means the day after today.
6. **listen** — Listen means pay attention to sound.
7. **easy** — Easy means not difficult.
8. **inside** — Inside tells us where the keys are.

## Speaking activity

Choose ten words from this lesson and speak for one minute. Try to include words about your family, home, work and daily routine. For example:

“My family lives in a small house. I go to work in the morning. I learn English every day. I sometimes read a book in the evening.”

Do not worry about speaking quickly. Focus on making clear, complete sentences.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many English words should a beginner learn daily?
Start with five to ten useful words. Learn their meanings and use them in your own sentences.

### Should I learn English words with meanings or sentences?
Learn both. A simple meaning helps you understand the word, while an example sentence shows how to use it.

### How can I remember vocabulary for a long time?
Revise words after one day and again after a few days. Use them in speaking and writing.

### Are these words enough to speak English?
They are a useful starting point, but speaking also requires sentence formation, listening, pronunciation and regular practice.
